AI makes Flutter a stronger choice, not a weaker one.

When AI makes working in Dart easier, "our team already knows JavaScript" becomes a less a compelling reason to default to frameworks like React Native or Electron.

And Flutter has a LOT  going for it:
- Stateful hot reload
- Excellent DevTools for debugging, profiling, and UI inspection
- One consistent UI codebase across mobile and desktop
- Native compiled apps without bundling Chromium

React Native and Electron have their strengths, but for a new cross-platform app, Flutter would is my first choice, every time.

AI makes writing code easier. It doesn't make developer experience, performance, or framework choice any less important.

Am I missing something, or is Flutter seriously underrated?

result.text:
Flutter is a 3D engine now. 99 seconds from my Flutter & Friends talk.

Everything in the cut is rendered by Flutter on the stable channel, on Impeller and Flutter GPU. No platform views, no native textures piped in from another engine, no custom fork. The engine is Flutter Scene, a complete 3D game engine for Flutter.

Complete means graphics, physics, audio, networking, an editor, and tools for AI coding agents, in one open source project. It runs on macOS, Linux, Windows, iOS, Android, web, and custom embedders. It scales down to a single model in a widget and up to full games, and dozens of contributors have landed work in it this year.

A scene is a widget. Put it in a Column, stack UI over it, or draw it transparent over the UI so physics objects cast shadows on your buttons. And hot reload works on the scene itself. Change a light or a material in Dart and it updates in place.

The full talk covers materials, lighting, the editor, and agent skills. Link in the reply. :)

data.translation:
I'm really happy to see everyone returning to Native in the LLM era.  
Evaluating a framework requires considering both the framework itself and the course of history.

React Native was already a fairly mature framework back in the day. Around 2020, KMP couldn't even handle UI, Jetpack Compose wasn't mature yet, and Flutter was even less reliable.

In contrast, React Native had the unique advantage of sharing code across Web, iOS, and Android. The toolchain provided by Facebook at the time was quite comprehensive, and Metro's hot reload offered a nice boost in development efficiency. There was even this magical framework called Reanimated that made animations sometimes simpler than native—though, of course, it came with a ton of bugs.

A lot of people evaluate a framework based solely on one isolated metric, but engineering is all about trade-offs. Promoting a framework in a company often means weighing all sorts of factors, not just the obvious ones like performance or syntax.

Take Shopify, for example—they're a Web powerhouse. Switching to React Native lets their massive Web team start contributing to mobile code, which brings huge efficiency gains and massive savings on human resources.

Some folks might not even realize this, but hiring Mobile Engineers abroad isn't easy at all. There just aren't that many Mobile Engineers out there, and the ones who make it to big tech are few and far between. Most engineers are frontend, backend, or Web full-stack. Plenty of teams can't even fill their headcount (HC) after a whole year. And that was during the pandemic hiring boom.

That said, I do think Meta, now positioning itself as a "model factory," is under massive economic pressure, so legacy tech like React Native probably isn't getting any extra resources. That might be a big reason why Shopify is leaning toward prioritizing Native.

data.translation:
Shopify Announces: Full Return to Native Development from React Native

Shopify was once a staunch supporter of React Native. In 2020, Shopify chose to go "All-in" and fully embrace React Native, achieving "write once, run everywhere" functionality. But now, Shopify is completely migrating all of its mobile applications from React Native back to Swift and Kotlin.

This decision is mainly due to the enhanced capabilities of AI in coding. Today's Coding Agents can directly take the iOS version of code and write the corresponding Android version, and vice versa.

AI can help developers break through the boundaries of tech stacks, enabling them to write in programming languages they aren't typically familiar with. It also ensures that applications on both platforms remain highly consistent through shared code standards, test cases, and code review mechanisms.

Moreover, with AI, the efficiency is remarkably high. Shopify's core shopping app Shop took just 12 weeks to complete the entire process—from initial proof of concept to a fully refactored native app that's now live on app stores. The refactoring work for Shopify's other apps is currently underway at a rapid pace.

而且借助 AI 效率很高，Shopify 的核心购物应用 Shop 仅仅用了 12 个星期，就完成了从最初的概念验证，到完全重构的原生 App 并在应用商店上架的整个过程。Shopify 其他应用的重构工作目前也在紧锣密鼓地推进中。
